headline: Drones Strike Three Ships Near Sulina Canal
subheadline: No casualties; crews controlled fires on board
insight: Drones hit tankers Evia Petrol V and Ali Najafov and bulker Marsol late on 14 Nov; two were struck 4-5 nm SE of Sulina in Romanian waters. No casualties, fires out.

factCheck.notes: CORROBORATED (Reuters via gCaptain re-checked 16 Nov 13:05; Euronews; Kyiv Post; MarEx): Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea named Evia Petrol V (Greek-flag oil/chemical tanker), Marsol (St Kitts & Nevis bulk carrier) and Ali Najafov (oil products tanker, St Kitts & Nevis per Reuters); struck late Sat 14 Nov; Evia Petrol V and Marsol 4 and 5 nm SE of the Sulina canal inside Romanian territorial waters; no casualties; crews controlled fires; jets scrambled twice (PM Luca Niculescu, 15 Nov). Separate strike on Palau-flag Larissa 1 late 13 Nov kept in description only. Romania did not name the launcher; Russia denies targeting Ukraine's neighbours, so no attribution on the card. Ali Najafov's position not published, hence 'two were struck'. Event date 14 Nov stated on card; not presented as new today.

image.credit: PH2 Elliot, U.S. Navy / Wikimedia Commons

meta.description: Drones struck three commercial ships near Romania's Sulina canal late on 14 November 2026: the Greek-flag oil and chemical tanker Evia Petrol V, the St Kitts and Nevis-flag bulk carrier Marsol and the oil products tanker Ali Najafov, Romanian Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea said. Evia Petrol V and Marsol were hit 4 and 5 nautical miles southeast of the canal inside Romanian territorial waters; there were no casualties and crews brought the fires on board under control, while Romania scrambled fighter jets twice. A separate drone strike hit the Palau-flag general cargo ship Larissa 1 in Romanian waters late on 13 November, also without injuries; Romania has not named who launched the drones.
